title: SB53 (2024 Regular): RELATING TO FIREARMS POSSESSION.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2024/bills/SB53_.HTM; sha256 dfca0ca2a9edee2ccf1acd25a8eefd090e0bf9ee2cc57c3fc4bd800bb7b88c75)
provenance.note: Introduced version; no votes on file, later amendments not in text read. In the bill's own words the text strikes 'voluntarily surrender' options and changes 'may' to 'shall' for police seizure (sections 2-5); those passages hold struck words and are not quoted. Section 4 (HRS 134-7.5) quote is the sentence on where seized firearms are taken; the bill also makes seizure after household assault mandatory.

operative_text:
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-7): No person who has been restrained pursuant to an order of any court, including a gun violence protective order issued pursuant to part IV, from contacting, threatening, or physically abusing any person, shall possess, control, or transfer ownership of any firearm or ammunition therefor, so long as the protective order, restraining order, or any extension is in effect, unless the order, for good cause shown, specifically permits the possession of a firearm and ammunition.
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-7.3): The chief of police shall search all applicable records to determine whether the applicant has been issued any permits to acquire or has registered any firearms.
SECTION 4 (HRS 134-7.5): Firearms seized under this section shall be taken to the appropriate county police department for safekeeping or as evidence.
SECTION 5 (HRS 806-11): At the time of arraignment, the court shall order a defendant who is under indictment for, or who has waived indictment for, or who has been bound over to the circuit court for a felony, or any crime of violence, or an illegal sale of any drug, to dispose of all firearms and ammunition within the defendant's possession in a manner in compliance with the provisions of chapter 134 and shall inform the defendant of the provisions of section 134-7(b) and section 134-12.5.
